findings.title: Embedded-post author link swaps the light and dark lightness values
findings.body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the conversion should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The changed line instead uses 70% for $primary and 30% for $secondary. Light themes therefore get a much paler color than before, and dark themes get the wrong muted shade, reducing contrast in both themes.

findings.title: Group-member name changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
findings.body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the conversion should keep 30% for the light-theme $primary branch and use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) for dark themes. The changed line uses 50% for both branches, making the name paler than intended on light themes and too dark/muted on dark themes.

findings.title: Custom-message-length swaps the light and dark lightness values
findings.body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), so the conversion should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The changed line instead uses 30% for $primary and 70% for $secondary. Light themes therefore get a much darker color than before, and dark themes get the opposite, overly light shade.

findings.title: Topic-map heading changes the original 20% lightness to 50%
findings.body: This .topic-map h3 rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), so the conversion should keep 20% for the light-theme $primary branch and use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%) for dark themes, as the corresponding desktop rule does. The changed line uses 50% for both branches, making the heading substantially paler on light themes and giving the wrong shade on dark themes.
